text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Scottish convict artist and diarist in early Australia THOMAS WATLING was born in 1762. He was convicted of forging banknotes, but his skill as an artist earned him an early pardon.
British author best known for "The Lord of the Flies" SIR WILLIAM GOLDING was born in 1911.
English actress ROSEMARY HARRIS , who gained recognition in "The Shiralee" and "Boys from Brazil", was born in 1930.
British fashion designer ZANDRA RHODES was born in 1940.

US singer MAMA CASS ELLIOT, who was part of the pop group 'The Mamas and the Papas', was born in 1941. She is probably best known for the way she died in 1974. She choked to death on a ham sandwich. Her solo hits included "Dream A Little Dream Of Me" (1968) and "It's Getting Better" (1969).

English actor JEREMY IRONS was born in 1948. His memorable roles include parts in "The French Lieutenant's Woman" and "Brideshead Revisited". He has gained a reputation as the "thinking woman's sex symbol".
TWIGGY (LESLEY HORNBY) was born in 1949. She came to prominence in the 1960s as the anorexic-looking English model in "The Boyfriend". She went on to became a star of stage and screen.
US actor, Broadway musical star and singer REX SMITH was born in 1955. His biggest hit was the million seller "You Take My Breath Away".

UK leadsinger with the 'Runaways' LITA FORD was born in 1958. In April 1984 she released a solo album and had a success with "Kiss Me Deadly" (1988) and "Close My Eyes Forever" (1989) a duet woth OZZY OSBOURNE.
** EVENTS **
1846 : English writer ELIZABETH BARRETT eloped to Paris

with fellow poet ROBERT BROWNING. They had been secretly married the day before. BARRETT was accompanied by her faithful maid WILSON and her spaniel FLUSH as she fled from London and the tyranny of her father.
1859 : The Confederate song "Dixie" was first sung by its
composer DANIEL DECATUR EMMETT, a black-faced ministrel in a New York theatre.
1876 : American inventor MELVILLE BISSELL patented the
carpet sweeper.
1888 : The world's first beauty contest was held in
Belgium. It was won by BERTHA SOUCARET who collected the five-thousand franc prize.
1905 : British doctor, philanthropist and founder of
homes for destitute children THOMAS BARNARDO died.
1928 : MICKEY MOUSE appeared on the screen for the first
time. MICKEY was the star of an animated cartoon feature "STEAMBOAT WILLIE" which opened at the Colony Theatre in New York.
1945 : Former US child-star SHIRLEY TEMPLE married JOHN
AGAR in Hollywood.
1952 : CHARLIE CHAPLIN was dubbed "subversive' by
rightwingers in the United States.
1966 : American singer JOAN BAEZ led black children to an
all-white school in Mississippi.
1977 : US film director ROMAN POLANSKI was jailed for
three months for having sex with a 13-year-old girl.
1981 : SIMON and GARFUNKEL reunited after 11 years to
play to an audience of 400,000 in New York's Central Park.
1982 : A Royal Commission into Australia's meat industry
found that meat inspectors substituted horse and kangaroo meat for beef.
1985 : A massive earthquake rocked Mexico City. The
earthquake measured 8.1 on the richter scale and was the worst this century to hit the city. Thousands were killed and buildings and homes devastated.
1989 : San Diego was awarded the America's Cup after the
New York Supreme Court reversed the decision of March that year to award the Cup to New Zealand.
1994 : A series of volcanos began erupting around Rabaul
in Papua New Guinea, forcing the evacuation of thousands of residents.
